formal_statement.lean_header:
theorem p01_t1_pairwise_nonnegative
    (fp : StandardAddModel) (r : ℕ) (v : Fin (2 ^ r) → ℝ)
    (hvalid : GammaValid fp.u r)
    (hv : ∀ i, 0 ≤ v i) :
    |pairwiseSum fp.fl_add r v - ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ r), v i| ≤
      gamma fp.u r * ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ r), v i
formal_statement.plain_language: For nonnegative inputs, the pairwise summation error is no larger than gamma(u,r) times the ordinary exact sum.

assumptions: Each rounded addition follows the shared standard addition rule.
The shared standard model also records exact addition from zero for a source-consistent common interface and for library adapters; the T1 pairwise computation does not use that field.
Overflow, underflow, and other exceptional machine behavior are outside the mathematical model.
informal_statement: For 2^r nonnegative inputs, the absolute error of balanced pairwise summation is at most gamma(u,r) times their exact sum.
informal_proof: Equation (3.6) gives gamma(u,r) times the sum of input absolute values because every input passes through r rounded additions. For nonnegative inputs each absolute value equals the input, so that sum is the ordinary exact sum.
tier_rationale: The task is a direct specialization of one general pairwise estimate. It requires finding and applying the general result and simplifying absolute values of nonnegative inputs.
